{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and angular dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use one-way ANOVA on the proportion or arcsine-transformed proportions, or equivalently logistic regression with paradigm as predictor; given the mean of 0.73, consider beta regression or quasi-binomial GLM if variance is heteroscedastic",
    "Given large sample size (n=76655), check for violations of normality using Shapiro-Wilk on residuals or Q-Q plots; if severe, use Welch's ANOVA or non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis followed by Dunn's test",
    "Report eta-squared or partial eta-squared for effect sizes",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect in a mixed-effects model (LMM) to account for clustering by subject (8 mice, unbalanced: SC21LM n=10986, SC21L1RF n=10972, etc.)"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If main effect of Stim Paradigm is significant, perform pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of paradigms for each response variable",
    "Use Tukey's HSD for balanced designs or Tukey-Kramer for unbalanced designs if ANOVA assumptions hold",
    "If using mixed models, use emmeans with Tukey adjustment or Satterthwaite/Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom",
    "For non-parametric alternatives, use Dunn's test with Bonferroni or FDR adjustment",
    "Report standardized mean differences (Cohen's d) or Hedges' g for each comparison"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Control family-wise error rate across the 10 pairwise comparisons per response variable using the Benjamin-Hochberg FDR procedure at alpha=0.05; given 5 response variables, consider controlling FDR across all 50 tests or use a hierarchical approach where Mauchly's/ANOVA must pass before post-hoc testing",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Stimulation paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels, making it unsuitable as an ordinary linear regression response. Recommend multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as the categorical response and the five performance variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) as predictors. This directly models P(Paradigm = k | performance). Alternatively, use Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) or Random Forest classification if non-linear relationships exist. Include Mouse as a stratification variable or random effect. Given class imbalance (Combined n=48846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3323), use class weights or SMOTE. Report confusion matrix, per-class precision/recall, and macro-averaged F1.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Residual Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests; note that n=76655 will likely reject normality even for minor deviations—focus on visual inspection and robustness",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equality of variances; given the wide ranges (Time-to-Target max=201.39, Path Efficiency max=29.82), variance likely differs by paradigm",
    "Independence: Check for within-mouse correlation using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); if ICC > 0.05, mixed model required",
    "Multicollinearity among predictors: Check VIF in predictive model; Success and Path Efficiency may correlate with Time-to-Target",
    "Outliers: Identify extreme values (e.g., Time-to-Target=201.39, Path Efficiency=29.82) and assess influence with Cook's distance",
    "Linearity: For multinomial logistic regression, check logit-linearity with Box-Tidwell or component-plus-residual plots"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation (n=48846, 63.7% of data) likely shows superior performance: lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, and lower AD compared to unimodal and Sham conditions",
    "ICMS Only may outperform visual-only conditions, given prior literature on direct cortical stimulation",
    "Sham (n=3505) expected to show poorest performance, serving as baseline for effect size estimation",
    "Bright Visual Only (n=3323) vs Dim Visual Only (n=9603) may differ in speed-accuracy tradeoff: brighter stimuli might yield faster but less accurate navigation",
    "AD expected to negatively correlate with Path Efficiency and Success, serving as a marker of circuit engagement",
    "Large effect sizes expected for Combined vs Sham; medium effects for Combined vs unimodal; small to medium effects between unimodal conditions"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance: Combined condition dominates (63.7% of trials), limiting power for comparisons involving Bright Visual Only (4.3%) and Sham (4.6%)",
    "Unbalanced mouse representation (SC21LM n=10986 vs SC11LM n=7233) may confound paradigm effects if certain mice disproportionately experienced specific paradigms",
    "Success is binary but treated as continuous in ANOVA; this is suboptimal—logistic mixed model preferred",
    "Path Efficiency and AD show extreme outliers (max values 29.82 and 1.0 vs means 0.47 and 0.38), suggesting long-tailed distributions that violate normality",
    "No temporal information: learning effects, fatigue, or session effects cannot be assessed from summary data",
    "Single temperature setting (0.75) and model (kimi) limit generalizability of any LLM-generated components",
    "Summary-only data view obscures trial-level structure and potential repeated-measures dependencies"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a multinomial logistic mixed-effects model with Stim Paradigm as categorical response, the five performance metrics as fixed-effect predictors (centered and scaled), and Mouse as random intercept; use Bayesian implementation (brms or rstanarm) with weakly informative priors to regularize estimates given class imbalance, and perform posterior predictive checks to assess classification accuracy and calibration across the five paradigms."
}
